Subject: Uptime matrix & on-call handoff — MSA / Order Form redlines

Samantha — thanks again for the redline. I pulled a few things together that I think will help speed legal and ops alignment: an uptime matrix that maps product tier to target, the service-credit calculation, and a proposed on-call handoff paragraph (who to page, phone escalation after 30 minutes, etc.). I'm attaching the PDF with inline suggestions.

High-level proposals:
- Uptime targets: Hosted API 99.9% (monthly), Dedicated 99.95% (monthly) — see matrix for edge-case scoring.
- Service credits: single-incident cap equal to 25% of monthly invoice; annual cap = 2x monthly invoice.
- Maintenance window: weekly 01:00–04:00 UTC, with 72h advance notice except emergency security patches.
- P1/P2 response times: P1 ack <= 15 minutes, P2 ack <= 1 hour; resolution SLAs are operational targets and credits only tied to measured downtime.

Next steps: can Laura provide legal-friendly language for the "excluded downtime" section (maintenance vs incident)? Can Aditya confirm the ack/resolution practicalities so we don't overpromise? Vanessa and I can coordinate the DocuSign/Order Form once text is settled.

Attachments: Novanet_MSA_redline_20270602.pdf (annotated)

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear summary and the annotated PDF. A few immediate notes from our side (we're combining input from legal and procurement):

- Novanet legal is asking for a firm production uptime of 99.9% for the Hosted plan (we may accept 99.95 for Dedicated but need language stating how and when Redwood can switch a customer between tiers).
- Credits: procurement prefers a monthly credit cap equal to 100% of the monthly invoice for persistent monthly downtime (not per-incident) — can you confirm if Redwood could accept that or propose an alternate cap?
- Measurement: we need the metric definition (how downtime is measured, region aggregation) so we can map to our monitoring.
- Maintenance: 72h notice is fine, but Novanet requires that maintenance not exceed 4 hours per maintenance window for production-critical customers and cannot occur during our business hours (M–F 08:00–18:00 local).

We attached Novanet’s suggested redline (separate file) and highlighted the clause about credits and measurement. Happy to take a 30-minute call to go line-by-line — Daniel and I are available Thu 10:00–11:30 PT or Fri 13:00–15:00 PT.

Samantha / Logan — I reviewed both your annotated PDF and Novanet's comments. Below are proposed legal-friendly edits; I'll produce a tracked-change doc by EOD.

Proposed legal bullets (summary):
- Definition of "Downtime": a Customer-perceived inability to successfully complete API requests due to Redwood service unavailability, measured as consecutive minutes where HTTP 5xx or connection failures exceed a 1% error rate across the affected region.
- Measurement: Redwood's telemetry (primary) with customer access to request logs. Measurement periods are UTC calendar month; regional incidents are credited only to affected region unless global impact is demonstrated.
- Scheduled Maintenance: standard weekly maintenance window of Sunday 01:00–04:00 UTC. For production-critical customers, scheduled maintenance shall not exceed 4 hours per scheduled window. Redwood will provide at least 72 hours' notice for non-emergency maintenance.
- Emergency Maintenance: may occur outside scheduled windows for security-critical fixes; Redwood will endeavour to notify customers within 2 hours of decision, and emergency maintenance will be excluded from downtime credits.
- Service Credits: credits calculated as (monthly recurring fee * downtime percentage). We can accept a monthly cap equal to 100% of the customer's monthly recurring fee only where Downtime exceeds 25% of the monthly billing period. For smaller outages, cap per incident at 25% of monthly fee; annual cap of credits not to exceed 200% of one month’s fee.
- Remedies: credits are customer's sole and exclusive remedy for SLA breaches.

I'll prepare language that allows Novanet to get the measurement transparency they request (log export access) while keeping the credit exposure bounded. If acceptable, I will circulate a tracked redline MSA + Order Form by EOD Wednesday.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quick ops confirmation from our side:
- P1 (service down, >90% requests failing): initial ack <= 15 minutes (pager), engineering triage within 30 minutes, customer updates every 60 minutes until resolution.
- P2 (severe degradation): initial ack <= 1 hour, engineering triage within 4 hours.
- P3: initial ack <= 4 hours.
- Scheduled maintenance: we can commit to 4-hour windows for production-critical tenants, provided we have maintenance orchestration lead time (automation requires ~48h to fully stage changes across instances).
- On-call handoff: Redwood uses a global on-call schedule — US engineers handle US region weekdays, EU engineers handle EU region weekdays; overnight coverage is global rotation. Handoff procedure: primary on-call posts summary and outstanding incidents in PagerDuty and a shared Slack channel; secondary takes ownership after explicit acknowledgement.

I'll attach the ops SLA matrix (spreadsheet) with observable metrics and the runbook excerpt. If Laura wants slightly different wording around "ack" vs "resolution" in the contract, happy to sync.

Attachments: ops_runbook_sla_matrix.xlsx
